_comment: Default Mandala keybindings. Copy this file to $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/mandala/keybinds.json (or $HOME/.config/mandala/keybinds.json) to override, or pass it explicitly with --keybinds <path>. On WASM, store a JSON object like this under localStorage['mandala_keybinds']. Missing fields fall back to the built-in defaults, so you only need to list the actions you want to change. Bindings are strings like 'Ctrl+Z', 'Shift+Alt+Delete', or 'Escape'. Modifier aliases: cmd/command/meta/super all mean Ctrl; option means Alt. Each action accepts a list, so you can bind multiple keys to the same action. Mouse gestures and the one touch gesture bind the same way: 'MiddleClick', 'Ctrl+RightDrag', 'LongPress'. fast_resize_start (Ctrl+RightDrag) is a mouse accelerator by design: to resize by touch on desktop, long-press a node (enter_resize_mode includes LongPress) and drag one of its handles with a finger; the browser has no touch resize yet. A binding naming a retired gesture, such as 'TwoFingerDrag', is skipped with a warning saying what replaced it. Payload-carrying actions take objects instead: "set_color": [{ "combo": "F1", "args": ["bg", "#fafafa"] }]. An unrecognized top-level *key* is ignored with a warning on stderr rather than rejected, so one stale key never costs you the rest of the file; keys starting with '_' are treated as comments and never warn. A recognized key holding a *malformed value* gets the same treatment: it keeps its built-in default with a warning naming it, and every other binding in the file still loads. A key written twice uses its last occurrence, also with a warning. Only a file that is not a JSON object at all is ignored whole.
